steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Laura? Fort Barron's nothing new to you, is it?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Oh... Sorry, I was just thinking about something...

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: I saw you staring at the model on the desk. You almost had me thinking maybe there was something wrong with it.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: I heard from the senior operators that the engineering team made this model as a memento, after Fort Barron's retrofit was completed and delivered.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: So, there's nothing wrong with it, right?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: It's fine. It looks... just like the base does now.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Good to hear. Shall we continue, then?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: I'm ready. Let me take a look at your report... Ahem...

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Laura, what did you do after you received the order to catch the bank robbers?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: At the time, I was leading the engineering team to double-check the structural integrity of the plate connection, and after we got the news...

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I chose to continue the work we were already doing.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Could you go into the reasoning behind your decision?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: The orders I received were that, aside from those participating directly in the plate's connection work, all other teams were to start pursuing the bank robbers.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: And I made the determination that the connection work still needed the manpower of our engineering team.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: So I chose to follow orders and not divert anyone from our work.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: But according to the report, one of the bank robbers was your partner at Davistown. Were you aware of that?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I... I knew about that, yeah.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Regarding that, what was your determination at the time?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Determination... My determination?

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: 'Don't make me repeat myself.'

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: My determination... I didn't make any...

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I'm an employee of Blacksteel, and following my orders...

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: ...is my responsibility.

steps.name: Blacksteel Mercenary
steps.text: (Frowns) ......

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: 'Following orders. Laura, you made the right decision.'

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: How's that? I do a pretty good impression, right?

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: And that 'Don't make me repeat myself' was, like, exactly the same, wasn't it?

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: *sigh* What's wrong, Laura? You look so out of it. It can't be because I'm putting too much pressure on you, can it?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: It's okay... I'm just...

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Please, let's just get back to it.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Um... That was the last question.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: I need to tell you this, Laura. Ever since we got back from Davistown, you've looked kind of uneasy.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: We all know that it was a very special operation, and you happened to be at the heart of the vortex.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: I really can't imagine what you went through, but even then, you can't let yourself be tied up by something like that.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: What you need now is rest.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Rest...

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: And some very good rest. So stop thinking about the mission report. You should apply for leave instead.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: You're right... I can't stay so depressed.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: So Aliza, can we do this again, please?

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: You haven't been listening at all, have you...?

steps.name: Blacksteel Mercenary
steps.text: If you ask me, you'd best forget about the report.

steps.name: Blacksteel Mercenary
steps.text: It's been two weeks. No one's ever going to bring it up again.

steps.name: Blacksteel Mercenary
steps.text: In the long history of the company, this was only a tiny interlude. You can be as serious about this as you want, but the supervisor's only going to pretend to be interested.

steps.name: Blacksteel Mercenary
steps.text: She's right. You should be asking them for a long vacation.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: No... I have to finish this report.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I was in Davistown from the start. I saw most of what happened with my own eyes. I experienced most of it personally.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: It's a Blacksteel employee's responsibility to execute their orders during a mission, and to compile a report on it afterwards. Besides...

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: You saw what I wrote, didn't you? Don't you think the higher-ups should be informed of everything that happened in an organized report?

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Laura, I...

steps.name: Blacksteel Mercenary
steps.text: Frankly, there's no need to report anything. What happened in Davistown couldn't be any clearer.

steps.name: Blacksteel Mercenary
steps.text: While completing a government-sanctioned mission, a Blacksteel employee participated in criminal activities and greatly damaged our company's image and reputation.

steps.name: Blacksteel Mercenary
steps.text: Everyone here already knows all that. It isn't something worth bringing up over and over again. Especially not... two weeks after the fact.

steps.name: Blacksteel Mercenary
steps.text: We need paychecks to put food on the table. We need to follow orders and not get fired.

steps.name: Blacksteel Mercenary
steps.text: So there's no reason for you to work yourself up over this.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I... I still think I want to talk to somebody.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Where does it hurt?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Nothing wrong with that. That's how you learn discipline.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Are you going to do it again?

a.text: I won't do it again, Mamá. I shouldn't have made a mess under the bed...
But... Mamá, I really love those machine parts. I know you don't like me playing with them, so I had to...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Sounds like you still don't realize what I'm punishing you for.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Follow me once you're done eating.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: What's the matter, Laura? You asked to talk to me all of a sudden.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Um, Franka, there's something I want your opinion on.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Is it about Davistown?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Is it that obvious?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Our little pistachio who's always cheering everyone up is suddenly acting all sulky. It'd be harder not to figure it out, don't you think?

spans.text: Our little pistachio who's always cheering everyone up is suddenly acting all sulky. It'd be harder
to figure it out, don't you think?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I put together a report on Davistown.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Liskarm already submitted one.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Like, a good while ago?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I know, but—

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Alright, I can more or less guess what you wrote in there.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: And I can tell you what's going to happen if you submit it.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: It'll be ignored, your issues won't be addressed, and if whoever has to read it is in a bad mood that day, you may even be disciplined.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: It's that simple.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: It's been two weeks, but sometimes I still think about what happened back there.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: All of us saw what was going on in Davistown. Jessica did so much for them, but even that wasn't enough for her.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Hasn't she always been like that though?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Franka... Do you think I did poorly in Davistown?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Wow, who knew pistachios were so rich in vitamin justice?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: This isn't about justice—

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: At least you two got to see her in the end. What was I doing while all that was going on...?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: She was in such a dangerous situation, but I was just hanging out on the ship.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Even though... Even though I really wanted to be with her...

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: 'We're wearing Blacksteel uniforms and following the orders of the higher-ups. It's not your fault if you weren't able to do something.'

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: If our good captain Liskarm were here, I'm sure she'd say that in the sincerest, most heartfelt way you ever heard.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Then, she'd probably give you a warm hug and make sure you knew you had someone to lean on aboard the landship.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Franka, are you—

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: All I'm saying is that if you turn around and go run into Liskarm's arms right about now, you'll get all the well-meaning advice and comfort you could ever want.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: But me? All you're gonna get from me is my sharp tongue and some finely aged sarcasm.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: ...I think that's what I want.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Alright then. Do you feel bad because you weren't able to help Jessica, or are you just jealous that she made a choice when you couldn't?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Did you write that report because you believe it's the truth, or are you just trying to convince yourself that you're not a coward?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I was born to a normal family. My mother is an ordinary doctor, but I didn't have a lot of freedom.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: My family moved from Bolívar to Columbia when I was younger. I managed to get into college, but then I caught Oripathy right before I graduated.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: None of the tech companies I was aiming for would give me a second glance. Blacksteel was the only place I could go.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: And when I got here, the first thing I learned was to follow orders and do whatever the rest of the team does.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I'm not jealous that she made a choice...

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: The name Brynley gave Jessica more trouble than it ever helped. We could all see that.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: So I'm not jealous of her wealth either. I know she carries a much bigger burden than I do.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: But that's exactly why I don't get it. How come Jessica was able to make that choice?
A silence falls between the two of them.
After some time, the brown-haired Vulpo looks up at the nightfall and breathes a sigh.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: So, if you'd gone after Jessica with us after you got that order, would you have pointed your gun at her?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I wouldn't.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: What if you were ordered to?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I still wouldn't.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Why not?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Because—

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I don't want to hurt her.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: So, don't you think you've already made a choice too?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: But, how's that—

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: How is it not?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: None of us are from a big, famous family like hers.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: When someone important makes a decision, it affects a lot of people, but for grunts like us, it doesn't have to matter to anyone but ourselves.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Is that really enough?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Why wouldn't it be?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Let's take a step back. Admitting that you just don't want to be a coward... would honestly be more honest than the truth.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: But isn't it important to tell the truth?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Sometimes, what's more important to the truth is being remembered.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: I'm just gonna throw this out there, so you just listen.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: You know that place called Rhodes Island, where Liskarm and I are dispatched—

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: The missions there are tough, but they offer some pretty nice benefits, and the people there are all pretty kind.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: If some little pistachio thinks there's no room in Blacksteel for her to grow...

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Then a change in soil isn't such a bad idea.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: ...Yeah.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Thanks, Franka.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Everyone always says that you're the lady to talk to about this sort of thing. And they're right.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Wait, hold up, what exactly are they saying about me?

spans.text: exactly are they saying about me?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: They all told me that Franka's got a foul mouth, but she'll help you solve your troubles.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Which numbskulls are out there ruining my street cred?!

a.text: Mamá, why are we... back in the room again?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Are you really interested in that equipment?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Then why didn't you just ask?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Right, I don't like it when you play with these parts, and I definitely don't want to see you end up like Grandma, holed up in the garage all day long.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: But you should've asked.

a.text: I was worried you'd say no...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Right, I could say no, but maybe I wouldn't have. There could be a different outcome, another choice.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: But if you never try, you'll never have another choice.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: You see that table? That's your workbench from now on. Take out everything you've been hiding under your bed.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Now!
Come in.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Boss.

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: Do you need me for something?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I'm sure you know that my last mission was in Davistown, right...?

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: I'm aware. What's up?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: About that, I wrote up a mission report as per protocol.

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: Since when did we have a protocol like that?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Well, we do...

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: Mission report... Oh, now I remember. Yeah, I guess you're right.

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: That was a big mission, with plenty of twists and turns. Good work getting a report out of all that.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: No, it’s nothing.

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: So I trust this will fill in a lot of blanks about the incident.
The man on the other side of the desk quickly reads through her report as she watches.
There's a sigh.
That's not what she expected.

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: This isn't what you should be writing reports on, Laura.

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: We're in charge of technology. There shouldn't be anything in here unrelated to our engineering work.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I understand that, but I saw so much more than that while carrying out my mission.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I can't pretend I didn't.

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: *sigh*

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: Whatever. No one's going to read this anyway, so it'll do.
He flips to the last page of the report and briskly signs his name.

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: You still have a long career ahead of you.

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: You really need to learn to sort out what you've seen and what you haven't.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Sorry, Chief, I'm just an engineer. I'm not too good at that sort of thing.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Which is why I have a request.

steps.name: Engineering Supervisor
steps.text: Go on.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: I want to apply for the next round of exchange projects and be dispatched to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: *cough* Let's continue, then.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: W-Wait. I'm not ready yet. Let me get myself together first...

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Okay, okay. Let's go.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Hm... So what's the story behind that puppet you carry on your waist?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: The puppet on my waist... What? Is that really an interview question?

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Of course it. It's right here in the Big Book of Interview Questions Franka gave me. 'Every now and then, interviewees should be asked questions about the accessories they're wearing.'

spans.text: Of course it. It's right here in the
Franka gave me. 'Every now and then, interviewees should be asked questions about the accessories they're wearing.'

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Alright then... My mother made me this, and I've been carrying it around ever since. Is that good enough?

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Shorter than the expected answer length, but it shouldn't be a problem.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Besides, you've already been through so many terrifying tests before this.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Didn't Franka tell you? As long as you pass the tests, the interview's just a formality and an excuse to chat. The way I see it, there's nothing to prep for.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: Oh, no no no. If I'm doing something, I've gotta do it right! I'm not taking any chances. Quick, next question!

spans.text: Oh, no no no. If I'm doing something, I've gotta do it
! I'm not taking any chances. Quick, next question!

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Ooh, this question seems pretty reliable...

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Laura! Let's hang out!

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Oh, are you studying for your Rhodes Island interview?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Looks like you've made up your mind.

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: What'd you expect? Shh, we'll talk later. Let me finish this question first.

steps.name: Blacksteel Clerk
steps.text: Laura, what are your thoughts on your future?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: My future?

steps.name: Laura
steps.text: My... future...

a.text: Mamá, do we really need to go?

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: It's too dangerous here, mija. We can't stay anymore. I don't want to see you grow up in a warzone.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: I don't want this either, but...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: A lot of times, we don't get to decide our own fate. I... I don't have a choice.

a.text: Choice... I don't get it. What's a choice...?
Please don't cry, Mamá... You still have me. I can make choices for you.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Yes, mija. Yes, you're my choice.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: Come, we'll go somewhere new, where you'll see a lot of new things, meet a lot of new people, and there will be a whole new fate waiting for you.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: One day, you'll find yourself between a rock and a hard place like this, and unsure of where the future will lead you.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: When that time comes, remember that as long as you keep moving forward, you'll find that your choice is there.

steps.name: Mother
steps.text: And this time, you'll be brave enough to make it.
